crit: Authors built their own 'real-world' intrusion datasets from University of Notre Dame network traffic to avoid the limitations of the DARPA'98 benchmark (synthetic normal traffic, 'not representative of contemporary network traffic'); two dataset types (packet-based and destination-based) were constructed so the approaches could be evaluated 'on datasets with different features and class distribution'.
notes: Two private datasets (Packets, Destinations) built by the authors from Notre Dame campus traffic and labelled with SNORT; Table I (p.2). Origin coded Binarised (authors) because SNORT attack types were collapsed into intrusive vs not ('treating this as a 2-class problem'); an adjudicator could instead read the datasets as created two-class (Natural). Fig. 1 (p.3) is a hand-drawn schematic, not an evaluation on generated data. The majority class is randomly undersampled to 1%-100% of its size to sweep ROC curves (p.4); this is part of the evaluated training procedure (RIPPER + undersampling), not coded as a data origin. No data release; the acknowledgment only thanks a colleague for allowing use of the data. Table I sums check (147+3933=4080; 2106+344,514=346,620). No IR printed. Results are ROC curves only (no tables).
